Topic: Cramer's Rule: A Geometric Perspective

Target audience: University students (Linear Algebra/Calculus)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area/Volume

Lecture lines:
The determinant is the signed area of a parallelogram.
Vectors form the sides of this geometric shape.
Area scaling helps us understand linear transformations.

Planned animations:
FadeIn a 2D square shape colored #FFFFFF to represent unit area.
Flash the square with #FFD700 to emphasize initial state.
Transform the square into a parallelogram using a determinant matrix.
Label the area formula 'Area = det(M)' in #00FFFF color.
Highlight the final geometric relationship in #FF4500 color.

Section: section_2 — Framing the Linear System

Lecture lines:
We represent Ax=b as a vector equation.
Scales x and y reach a target point b.
Think of reaching a crumb using two paths.

Planned animations:
FadeIn a set of vectors representing linear equations.
Animate vectors into a matrix block structure in #FFFFFF.
Highlight variables 'x' and 'y' using #00FF00.

Section: section_3 — Geometric Substitution

Lecture lines:
Replace a column with the target vector b.
New parallelograms emerge from this replacement.
Area ratios reveal the needed scale factors.
The ratio gives x for the first column.
This process defines Cramer's elegant rule.

Planned animations:
FadeIn a grid representing the coordinate system in #808080.
Slide the transformed parallelogram along the vector path.
FadeIn the replacement area symbol in #FFD700.

Section: section_4 — Visualization of the Solution

Lecture lines:
Visualize the parallelogram area changing dynamically.
The expansion factor directly represents coordinate x.
This visually confirms the determinant ratio identity.
Shrinking areas show lower coordinate values.
Expanding areas show higher coordinate values.

Planned animations:
FadeIn the intersection point of vectors in #FF4500.
Draw lines connecting the point to axes in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the resulting coordinates with a glowing effect #00FFFF.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Geometric Intuition

Lecture lines:
Cramer's Rule is a geometric ratio of space.
Solvability requires non-zero determinant area.
Flat space prevents reaching the target point.

Planned animations:
FadeIn all previous geometric steps side-by-side in #FFFFFF.
Pulse the final summary formula in #FFD700.
Fade out all elements to black #000000.

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(poly))
